title: Treaty of Muwatalli II with Alaksandu of Wilusa (CTH 76)
note: Vassal treaty from the Hattusa archives, c. 1280 BCE (Mesihović 2022); historical preamble on Hatti–Wilusa relations, military-aid clause (Easton et al. 2002, citing Beckman 1996 no. 13). Pin at Hattusa with an arc to Hisarlık; needs a primary translation (Beckman, Hittite Diplomatic Texts) and the Hethitologie Portal CTH entry.

title: Arzawa lands of western Anatolia (Arzawa, Mira, Seha River land, Hapalla, Wilusa)
note: Luwian-speaking kingdoms known almost only from Hittite texts; capital Apasa (Ephesus); conquered by Mursili II; Karabel relief and Hawkins's geography (Easton et al. 2002). Under-recorded Bronze Age Anatolian peoples.

title: Hattusa (Boğazköy), Hittite capital
note: UNESCO WHC 377; investigated since 1906 (Easton et al. 2002); archive of cuneiform tablets naming Wilusa and Ahhiyawa; Büyükkale citadel compared with Troy VI by Jablonka and Rose (2004). Needs a model (importance ≥ 3).

title: Discovery of 'Priam's Treasure' at Hisarlık and its dispersal
note: Found 31 May 1873; smuggled to Greece; Ottoman lawsuit settled for 10,000 gold francs; given to Berlin 1881; taken to the USSR in 1945; revealed 1994; Duma resolution 1998 (Staatliche Museen zu Berlin). Wartime looting and restitution thread; needs Pushkin Museum and Turkish perspectives. Domain may be better as art_music_literature or law_politics_rights.

title: Late Bronze Age collapse in the eastern Mediterranean
note: Fall of Mycenaean palaces (end LH IIIB, c. 1190 BCE per Rutter's Dartmouth chronology), Hittite Empire, Ugarit; Troy VIIa ends in fire c. 1200–1175 BCE. Regions geometry across Anatolia, the Levant, Cyprus, Egypt and Greece; causes contested (drought, earthquakes, Sea Peoples, systems collapse) as perspectives.
